::: {.hero-intro}
## I study how work and relationships change—and how inequality is reproduced.

My research combines network science, formal models, computational experiments, and longitudinal data to understand unequal change in labor markets and social ties.
:::

::: {.home-research-grid}
::: {.home-research-card}
<span class="research-index">01</span>

### Work, skills & technology

Work is changing. Not evenly. I study how skills and tasks diffuse across the occupational hierarchy amid technological change.
:::

::: {.home-research-card}
<span class="research-index">02</span>

### Relational persistence

A tie is never just a dyad. I examine when available alternatives destabilize relationships and shape who replaces whom.
:::

::: {.home-research-card}
<span class="research-index">03</span>

### Mobility & inequality

Where people can move depends on where they stand. I study relational constraints on urban and intergenerational mobility.
:::
:::
